$comment: Mechanical trust gate for learned collectors. A command the model discovers at run time is persisted to a project's .dashboard/profile.json and re-executed on later runs ONLY if it matches here: token-exact prefix, no shell metacharacters, no write-escape flags. Anything else runs once with explicit approval and is never stored. Scope boundary, stated plainly: this stops a stored command from quietly becoming a different command between runs. It is not a sandbox and does not confine what an allowed command may read.
$allow_comment: Token-exact prefixes. A prefix must be specific enough that no write subcommand shares it: 'git stash list' not 'git stash', 'gh api -X GET' not 'gh api', 'git branch --list' not 'git branch'.
$deny_comment: Substrings that void a match outright, checked before prefix matching. Shell metacharacters would let an allowed prefix carry an arbitrary second command; the flag entries are the known write/exec escapes inside otherwise read-only tools (git log --output=FILE writes a file; --exec and --upload-pack run a program).
$limit_comment: A stored collector command is a one-liner. Anything longer is not a collector.
